name: dmr
label: DMR / P25 / NXDN (dsd-fme)
description: Digital voice: DMR call metadata (talkgroup, radio ID, colour code, talker alias) from Ferrite's native decoder — runs node-side or in the browser — plus decoded speech via the user-installed dsd-fme helper (DMR, P25, NXDN, D-STAR, YSF).
ai_notes: Digital voice (DMR, P25, NXDN, D-STAR, YSF, dPMR) on a single conventional channel. Two decoders share the FmDemod tap: DmrDecode (pure Rust, WASM-able) reports DMR calls (`call` with slot/TG/source/CC/ENC — voice LC header or embedded LC late entry — `end` with duration, `alias`, `sync`); DsdHelper runs the operator-installed `dsd-fme` binary (not shipped with Ferrite: AMBE vocoder patents) on raw discriminator audio at 48 kHz and plays its synthesised speech; its `voice` start/stop records join the same `ui:dsd` Journal (its own call records are off, `metadata:false`; turn them on for P25/NXDN/D-STAR/YSF metadata, which DmrDecode doesn't parse yet). Verified 2026-10-13 from bigear on Antenna B, gain 40: 441.850 MHz DMR repeater (colour code 1; slot 2 TG 31068, slot 1 TG 93 North America; busy, talker aliases), also TG 31068 traffic on 440.125 and 440.5875 MHz. Tune to a repeater OUTPUT: US amateur DMR 440–450 MHz (e.g. 441–445 MHz, Brandmeister / DMR-MARC), public-safety P25 conventional 150–174 / 450–470 / 769–775 MHz, NXDN business 450–470 MHz. Antenna B at 440 MHz, gain 40; use `status.health` and the wide waterfall to find a 12.5 kHz channel with a flat-topped 4FSK block, then `tune` on-centre (`chan_shift_hz` must stay well inside the 48 kHz channel). Encrypted P25/DMR shows events but no audio. `mode=auto` is fine; set `dmr` / `p25` when the auto-detect flips between sync types. Output: `tail decoder --category dsd`; `await dsd`.
